description: Fix inconsistent font sizes and content that clips off buttons/containers on the mobile web UI. The design system defines a single 6-level type scale (meta/body/nav/lead/subhead/head/display) and intent-named spacing in tailwind.config.ts, with meta FLOORED at 0.75rem/12px. ux-audit-findings.md records (F6, F7, F32) that a codebase-wide sweep of arbitrary text-[..] bracket sizes was deliberately NOT done and that several permanent-chrome sites still use 11px (text-[0.6875rem]) values bypassing the meta floor. This feature does the targeted sweep: replace arbitrary/off-scale font sizes with scale tokens and fix clipping (text overflowing buttons, labels wrapping raggedly, truncation) - prioritising mobile-visible surfaces.
steps: Inventory off-scale font sizes: grep the app for arbitrary text sizes - `text-\[` bracket values and raw Tailwind sizes like text-xs/text-[10px]/text-[0.625rem]/text-[0.6875rem]/text-[0.8125rem]/text-[0.9375rem] - across app/ and components/. Cross-reference the specific sites named in ux-audit-findings.md F32 (components/layout/MobileBottomNav.tsx:105; components/listings/ListingActionIcon.tsx:53 `text-[0.6875rem] sm:text-xs`; app/listings/[id]/page.tsx around :302/:315/:329 StarRating and identity dl) and F7/F6 (ItemCard catalog variant). Produce a list of files/lines to change.

Replace each off-scale value with the nearest design-system token from tailwind.config.ts fontSize: use `text-meta` (0.75rem, the floor for chrome/badges/timestamps/counts), `text-body` (0.875rem, default copy/labels/fields), `text-nav` (sidebar rail only - do NOT use elsewhere), `text-lead`/`text-subhead`/`text-head`/`text-display` for titles per their documented intent. Anything currently below 12px must rise to at least `text-meta`. Do NOT introduce new bracket sizes and do NOT add new tokens unless genuinely missing (if a gap is found, document it rather than inventing a value).

Fix content clipping off buttons and containers: audit buttons and chips whose labels overflow or get cut (e.g. the item-detail action row grid where 'Report listing' wraps to two lines while 'Buy' does not - ux-audit F23 area, app/listings/[id]/page.tsx grid-cols-5). Ensure button labels either fit, wrap cleanly, or truncate with an accessible full label; prefer the existing Button component sizing. Look for fixed-height/overflow-hidden containers that clip text on a 320-375px viewport and for horizontal overflow in rows. Use existing utilities (line-clamp, truncate, min-w-0, flex-wrap) consistent with how the codebase already handles this.

Keep the diff mechanical and low-risk: change class strings only; do not restructure components beyond what a clipping fix requires. Where the audit file already prescribes a specific fix for a cited finding, follow it. Verify visually-reasoned changes against the token comments in tailwind.config.ts (e.g. iOS focus-zoom note - do NOT reintroduce a per-field 16px floor; fields intentionally use body).
If any component sets its own text size that would override a primitive's size (per F19's note about CatalogControls/ItemForm/AddPaymentMethodForm), make those consistent with the scale too.

Add a lightweight guard test if the project has a pattern for it (there are 'agreement' style tests): consider a unit test that scans a small set of the touched chrome components' source for banned sub-12px bracket sizes, OR extend an existing style test. If no clean pattern exists, skip the test rather than inventing a brittle one, and rely on the mechanical review. Record the decision in findings.
acceptance_criteria: No app/ or components/ source uses a font-size below 0.75rem (12px); the sites named in ux-audit-findings.md F32 no longer use text-[0.6875rem]-style values.
Off-scale arbitrary text bracket values on mobile-visible surfaces are replaced with design-system scale tokens (meta/body/nav/lead/subhead/head/display) without inventing new sizes.
The item-detail primary action row and other cited buttons no longer clip or ragged-wrap their labels at 320-375px widths (fits, clean wrap, or accessible truncation).
No visual regression to desktop sizing (sm: and up preserved where it already existed).
typecheck, lint (no new errors), and the full unit/component test suite (minus the 8 pre-existing Flutter failures) stay green.
verification: npm test (no regressions beyond the 8 pre-existing Flutter-agreement failures)
grep to confirm no remaining sub-12px bracket font sizes in the swept surfaces
findings:
The codebase had already been refactored substantially since the ux-audit was written, so most cited sites/paths in the plan were STALE. Verified state before changing anything:
- The item-detail page moved to app/(workspace)/listings/[id]/page.tsx (plan said app/listings/[id]/page.tsx). Its F23 grid-cols-5 + ListingActionIcon action row is GONE: Buy is now a full-width primary <Button>, Trade/Offer are icon-only 44px secondaries, and Report was demoted to the mobile-chrome header. F23 is [x] Addressed in ux-audit-findings.md and no longer clips/ragged-wraps at 320-375px. ListingActionIcon.tsx is now dead/unimported and already uses text-body (not text-[0.6875rem]).
- MobileBottomNav.tsx already uses text-meta with truncate; the F32-cited text-[0.6875rem] there was already removed.
- ListingActionIcon.tsx :53 text-[0.6875rem] sm:text-xs cited by F32 was already removed.

Actual remaining sub-12px / off-scale bracket sizes found via a full grep of app/ components/ lib/ (three sites, all permanent chrome bypassing the meta floor per F6/F7/F32):
  1. app/globals.css:403 .cardtrade-eyebrow/.market-label used text-[0.6875rem] (11px) -> text-meta.
  2. components/layout/mobile-chrome/variants.tsx:84 filter-active count badge text-[10px] -> text-meta; also bumped the circle size-3.5 -> size-4 so a 12px digit does not clip (clipping fix per step 3).
  3. components/messages/InboxThreadList.tsx:71 unread-count badge text-[10px] -> text-meta (its size-4/min-h-4 circle already fits 12px).
After the sweep, grep confirms ZERO text-[ bracket font sizes remain in app/components/lib.

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE (out of scope per plan step 4 / config comments):
- Form-field primitives (input.tsx, textarea.tsx, PlacePicker.tsx, SocialLinksEditor.tsx, DisputeEvidencePanel.tsx) use `text-base pointer-fine:text-body`. text-base is 16px (NOT sub-12px, a standard token) and is the deliberate F19 iOS focus-zoom solution; the plan explicitly says do NOT reintroduce/alter a per-field 16px floor and fields intentionally use body. NOTE for a future task: the `pointer-fine:` variant is used at 8 call sites but is NOT defined in tailwind.config.ts (its comment says it was removed with no call sites left) - so `pointer-fine:text-body` currently emits no CSS and those fields render at text-base/16px everywhere. This is a pre-existing inconsistency between the config comment and the field source, documented rather than changed because reconciling it (field sizing / iOS zoom) is a behavioral change beyond this font-consistency/clipping sweep.

GUARD TEST: added tests/unit/typeScaleFloor.test.ts (3 tests) following the mobileReleaseSourceAbsence source-absence pattern - it parses the swept surfaces + F32-named primitives, converts any text-[..] bracket size to px, and asserts none is below the 12px meta floor, with a self-check that it actually reads the files (refuses vacuous passes). Scoped to swept surfaces, not a codebase-wide ban (F6 explicitly did not take that on).

VERIFICATION: npm run typecheck clean; npm run lint unchanged from baseline (1 pre-existing error in scripts/lib/mobileContract.ts + 3 warnings incl. 2 pre-existing in ProposeTradeDialog.tsx which I did not touch); npm test = 874 passing (871 baseline + 3 new guard tests), only the 8 pre-existing Flutter-agreement failures remain (mobileDomainAgreement 3 + mobileThemeAgreement 5). The window.matchMedia uncaught errors in addPaymentMethodDialog.test.tsx are PRE-EXISTING (confirmed by git-stashing my changes and re-running: same errors on base, test file still passes). npm run build compiles + typechecks clean and fails only at /sitemap.xml prerender (missing Supabase env), the accepted non-regression.
